answer:
Solve the 2D heat equation u_t = 0.05*(u_xx + u_yy) on the domain x in [0,1] (Dirichlet) and y in [0,1) (periodic) for t in [0, 0.3].
Use alpha = 0.05 as the diffusion coefficient.
Apply Dirichlet boundary conditions u(0,y,t)=0 and u(1,y,t)=0.
Apply periodic boundary conditions in y: u(x,0,t)=u(x,1,t) with matching first derivative.
Use the initial condition u(x,y,0) = sin(pi*x)*cos(2*pi*y).
Use a tensor-product grid: x has Nx=60 uniform intervals giving 61 grid points x_i = i*(1/60) for i=0..60 with dx=1/60; y has Ny=64 uniform grid points y_j = j*(1/64) for j=0..63 with dy=1/64.
Discretize spatial derivatives with 2nd-order central differences: use periodic wrap-around indices in the y-direction and fixed zero values at the x-boundaries.
Integrate in time with Implicit Euler using dt=0.001 for exactly 300 time steps, ending at T=0.3.
At each time step solve the resulting sparse linear system (I - 0.05*dt*L) u^{n+1} = u^n, where L is the discrete 2D Laplacian assembled from the central-difference stencles with the stated boundary handling.
The unknown vector at each step contains only the 59 interior x-points (i=1..59) crossed with all 64 y-points, giving a system of size 3776.
Compute the final solution u(x,y,T=0.3) on the full 61-by-64 grid (including the zero-valued Dirichlet boundaries).
Save the file "solution_agent_heat_16.npz" containing: x (1D array of 61 values), y (1D array of 64 values), u (2D array of shape (64, 61) where u[j,i] = u(x[i], y[j])), and scalar metadata T=0.3, dx=1/60, dy=1/64, dt=0.001.
Save a heatmap or contour plot of u(x,y,T=0.3) as the file "solution_agent_heat_16.png".
Print the minimum value of u, the maximum value of u, and the discrete L2 norm sqrt(sum(u^2)*dx*dy) at T.
Evaluate the exact solution u_exact(x,y,t) = exp(-0.05*(pi^2 + 4*pi^2)*t)*sin(pi*x)*cos(2*pi*y) on the same grid at T=0.3.
Compute and print the maximum absolute error max|u_num - u_exact| and the discrete L2 error sqrt(sum((u_num - u_exact)^2)*dx*dy) at T.
